name: Recursively Nested Maximum Sequences Give Product Parents
statement: Suppose $C$ has a rank-$r$ maximum parent $M\in\mathcal D_k$, while $D$ has a rank-$s$ maximum parent $N$ lying in a complete maximum sequence whose entry function has a common nested-coordinate recursion. Then $C\times D$ has a rank-$(r+s)$ maximum parent in $\mathcal D_k$ with at most $r+s$ new auxiliary coordinates beyond the supplied marks.
proof: Extend $M$ to a complete maximum sequence in the same decomposition level. Delay its upper levels $s$ times and delay the second sequence $r$ times; delay preserves the common nested recursion. The disjoint level-sum class at rank $r+s$ is maximum. Threshold induction along the nested recursion keeps it in $\mathcal D_k$, and the zero delay face is exactly the product of the supplied parents, so their old marks recover $C\times D$.
